newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Rivaud group eyes AOM buy with BA.
newsitem.headline: French Rivaud group eyes AOM buy with BA.

text.p: The private Rivaud group and not the Bollore Group, would be interested in buying the AOM airline with British Airways Plc (BA) if it came up for sale, a spokeswoman for Bollore said on Friday.

She was commenting on an interview in newspaper Les Echos with Jean-Paul Parayre, a senior executive in the Rivaud group headed by Vincent Bollore. Parayre is also deputy chairman and managing director of trading company Bollore Technologies.
The newpaper quoted Parayre as saying, "If one day AOM were for sale, in conditions of transparency, we would without doubt be a candidate with British Airways for the purchase."
Bollore Technologies is not involved in the airline business, the spokeswoman said.
The Rivaud group, which includes the private Banque Rivaud, is partnering BA in a bid for the collapsed Air Liberte airline. Rivaud would own 30 percent of Air Liberte and BA 70 percent.
AOM is owned by the CDR state-backed holding company which is selling of former assets of Credit Lyonnais.
Rivaud has not started talks on AOM, the spokeswoman said.
